title: Analog Circuits (OP-AMP)

notes.heading: 1. Ideal OP-AMP Specifications, CMRR & Slew Rate
notes.proseLatex: An ideal operational amplifier has open-loop differential gain $A_{\text{OL}} = \infty$, input impedance $R_{\text{in}} = \infty$ (so input terminal currents are $i_+ = i_- = 0$), output impedance $R_{\text{out}} = 0$, bandwidth $\text{BW} = \infty$, $\text{CMRR} = \infty$, and slew rate $\text{SR} = \infty$ (practical IC 741: $A_{\text{OL}}\sim 10^5,\; R_{\text{in}}\sim 2\text{ M}\Omega,\; R_{\text{out}}\sim 75\,\Omega,\; \text{SR}\approx 0.5\text{ V}/\mu\text{s}$). Common-Mode Rejection Ratio is $\text{CMRR} = \left|\frac{A_d}{A_{\text{cm}}}\right|$ ($20\log_{10}|A_d/A_{\text{cm}}|\text{ dB}$). Slew rate $\text{SR} = \left|\frac{dv_o}{dt}\right|_{\max}$ limits undistorted sinusoidal peak $V_m$ at frequency $f$ via $2\pi f V_m \le \text{SR}$.

keyFormulas.label: CMRR (dB) & Slew-Rate Undistorted Frequency Limit
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Calculate CMRR in dB and maximum undistorted sine-wave frequency/amplitude.

examples.problemLatex: An op-amp has differential gain $A_d = 10^5$ and common-mode gain $A_{\text{cm}} = 0.1$. Find its $\text{CMRR}$ in $\text{dB}$.

notes.heading: 2. Virtual Short & Inverting, Non-Inverting, Buffer & Summing Gains
notes.proseLatex: ONLY under NEGATIVE feedback (output fed back to the $-$ input without rail saturation!), high $A_{\text{OL}}$ forces the virtual-short condition $v_- = v_+$ together with $i_- = i_+ = 0$. Grounding $v_+ = 0$ creates a virtual ground at $v_- = 0$, giving: Inverting amplifier $v_o = -\frac{R_f}{R_1}v_{\text{in}}$ (input resistance $= R_1$); Summing amplifier $v_o = -R_f\sum\frac{v_k}{R_k}$; Non-inverting amplifier $v_o = \left(1 + \frac{R_f}{R_1}\right)v_{\text{in}}$; and Voltage Follower / Buffer ($R_f = 0, R_1 = \infty \implies A_v = +1$, high $Z_{\text{in}}$ to low $Z_{\text{out}}$ impedance matching!).

keyFormulas.label: Inverting, Non-Inverting, Summing & Subtractor Equations
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Solve any op-amp resistor network in 15 seconds via v- = v+ and KCL at node v-.

examples.problemLatex: In a non-inverting op-amp circuit powered by $\pm 15\text{ V}$ rails, $R_1 = 2\text{ k}\Omega$, $R_f = 8\text{ k}\Omega$, and $v_{\text{in}} = +2\text{ V}$. Find $v_o$.
stepsLatex: $v_o = 5 \times 2\text{ V} = +10\text{ V}$ (within $\pm 15\text{ V}$ rails, so linear!).

notes.heading: 3. Integrator, Differentiator, Comparator & Schmitt Trigger
notes.proseLatex: Replacing feedback $R_f$ with capacitor $C$ creates an inverting INTEGRATOR $v_o(t) = -\frac{1}{RC}\int v_{\text{in}}\,dt$ (converts a square wave into a TRIANGULAR wave, acting as a low-pass filter); swapping $R$ and $C$ creates a DIFFERENTIATOR $v_o(t) = -RC\frac{dv_{\text{in}}}{dt}$ (high-pass, amplifies high-frequency noise). Open-loop or POSITIVE feedback drives output to $\pm V_{\text{sat}}$: an open-loop comparator switches at one threshold, whereas a positive-feedback Schmitt trigger introduces HYSTERESIS ($V_{\text{UTP}} \neq V_{\text{LTP}}$) for noise immunity and converts sine waves into clean square waves!

keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Predict square/triangular waveform conversions and closed-loop bandwidth.

wbjeebTraps: POSITIVE feedback vs NEGATIVE feedback trap: ALWAYS check whether $R_f$ connects to the $-$ terminal (linear virtual short!) or the $+$ terminal (Schmitt trigger saturating at $\pm V_{\text{sat}}$ — virtual short FAILS!).
Supply rail clipping: even in a linear amplifier with gain $+10$, if $v_{\text{in}} = 2\text{ V}$ and rails are $\pm 12\text{ V}$, output clips at $+12\text{ V}$ (NOT $+20\text{ V}$)!
Remember the $+1$ in non-inverting gain $1 + R_f/R_1$ (can NEVER have magnitude $< 1$, unlike inverting $-R_f/R_1$).

conceptPrimer.heading: Ideal OP-AMP Specs — and the Real 741
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Ideal: $A_{\text{OL}} = \infty$, $R_{\text{in}} = \infty$ (so $i_+ = i_- = 0$), $R_{\text{out}} = 0$, BW $= \infty$, CMRR $= \infty$, slew rate $= \infty$. Practical IC 741: $A_{\text{OL}} \sim 10^5$, $R_{\text{in}} \sim 2\ \text{M}\Omega$, $R_{\text{out}} \sim 75\ \Omega$, SR $\approx 0.5\ \text{V}/\mu\text{s}$. Micro-check: with $A_{\text{OL}} = 10^5$, holding $v_o = 10\ \text{V}$ linearly needs $v_d \approx 100\ \mu\text{V}$ — the virtual short in the flesh.

conceptPrimer.heading: CMRR and Slew Rate
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $\text{CMRR} = \left|\frac{A_d}{A_{\text{cm}}}\right|$, quoted as $20\log_{10}(\cdot)$ dB — rejection of the common signal both inputs share. Slew rate $\text{SR} = \left|\frac{dv_o}{dt}\right|_{\max}$ caps the largest undistorted sine: $2\pi f V_m \le \text{SR} \Rightarrow f_{\max} = \frac{\text{SR}}{2\pi V_m}$. Micro-check: SR $= 0.5\ \text{V}/\mu\text{s}$, $V_m = 5\ \text{V}$: $f_{\max} = \frac{0.5\times10^6}{2\pi\times5} \approx 15.9\ \text{kHz}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Virtual Short: Bought Only by Negative Feedback
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: With NEGATIVE feedback (output to the $-$ input) and huge $A_{\text{OL}}$, the differential input is driven to nearly zero: $v_- = v_+$, and with $R_{\text{in}} = \infty$ no input current flows. Grounding $v_+$ makes $v_-$ a VIRTUAL GROUND. POSITIVE feedback (to $+$) destroys the virtual short — the output saturates and hysteresis rules instead. Micro-check: every linear op-amp circuit you solve starts by writing $v_- = v_+$ and KCL at that node.

conceptPrimer.heading: Inverting Amplifier and the Virtual Ground
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: With $v_+ = 0$: $v_o = -\frac{R_f}{R_1}v_{\text{in}}$; the input resistance is exactly $R_1$ (the source looks into the virtual ground). The summing amplifier extends this: $v_o = -R_f\left(\frac{v_1}{R_1} + \frac{v_2}{R_2}\right)$ — a weighted summer whose weights are resistor ratios. Micro-check: $R_f = 10\ \text{k}\Omega$, $R_1 = 2\ \text{k}\Omega$: gain $-5$, and the source sees $2\ \text{k}\Omega$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Non-Inverting Amplifier and the Buffer
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: The signal drives $v_+$ directly: $v_o = \left(1 + \frac{R_f}{R_1}\right)v_{\text{in}}$ — gain at least $+1$, high input impedance (the source never sees a resistor ladder). $R_f = 0$, $R_1 = \infty$ collapse it to the voltage follower / buffer ($A_v = +1$): high-$Z$ to low-$Z$ impedance matching without amplification. Micro-check: $R_1 = 2\ \text{k}\Omega$, $R_f = 8\ \text{k}\Omega$: gain $+5$; $v_{\text{in}} = 2\ \text{V}$ on $\pm15\ \text{V}$ rails $\Rightarrow v_o = +10\ \text{V}$, still linear.

conceptPrimer.heading: Integrators, Differentiators, Comparators and Schmitt Triggers
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Replace $R_f$ with $C$: inverting integrator $v_o = -\frac{1}{RC}\int v_{\text{in}}dt$ — square wave in, TRIANGLE out (a low-pass flavour). Swap R and C: differentiator $v_o = -RC\frac{dv_{\text{in}}}{dt}$ (high-pass, noise-hungry). Open-loop or positive feedback drives $v_o$ to $\pm V_{\text{sat}}$: a bare comparator switches at one threshold, while the Schmitt trigger adds HYSTERESIS ($V_{\text{UTP}} \ne V_{\text{LTP}}$) for noise immunity — sine in, clean square out. Micro-check: integrator on a square wave: flat top integrates to a ramp — triangle.

keyDefinitions.definition: High-gain differential DC amplifier intended for closed-loop feedback operation.
Condition $v_- \approx v_+$ with zero input current, forced by high gain under negative feedback.
Virtual short with $v_+$ grounded: $v_- \approx 0$ though no current flows to earth.
Ratio of differential to common-mode gain, $|A_d/A_{\text{cm}}|$, usually in dB.
Maximum output voltage slope, $|dv_o/dt|_{\max}$, limiting large-signal speed.
Open-loop stage swinging to $\pm V_{\text{sat}}$ according to the differential input sign.
Positive-feedback comparator with hysteresis thresholds $V_{\text{UTP}}$ and $V_{\text{LTP}}$.
Two different switching thresholds depending on direction of travel — noise rejection.
Constant $f_t$: closed-loop gain times its bandwidth.

memoryHooks: Ideal six-pack: gain, $R_{\text{in}}$, BW, CMRR, SR all $\infty$; $R_{\text{out}} = 0$.
No virtual short without negative feedback — check the $R_f$ node first.
Inverting looks into $R_1$; non-inverting looks into infinity.
Gain $\times$ bandwidth $= f_t$ — pay for one with the other.
Integrator squares to triangles; differentiator is the noise magnet.
Schmitt = comparator + hysteresis: two thresholds, one clean square.
$f_{\max} = \text{SR}/2\pi V_m$ — slew decides the biggest clean sine.
Rails are the ceiling: $\pm V_{\text{sat}}$ clips before the math does.
commonMistakes: Applying the virtual short under positive feedback (Schmitt/comparator).
Forgetting the rail clip: ideal math giving $20\ \text{V}$ on $\pm12\ \text{V}$ rails.
Calling the inverting input resistance $\infty$ (it is $R_1$).
Expecting a differentiator to clean noise (it amplifies it).
Swapping $V_{\text{UTP}}$/$V_{\text{LTP}}$ roles or claiming they are equal.
Treating CMRR as a linear ratio in a dB answer.
Using an integrator as a high-pass filter.
examChecklist: Check the feedback path: negative $\to$ virtual short; positive $\to$ saturation.
Solve linear circuits with $v_- = v_+$ and KCL at the node.
State the inverting stage's input resistance $= R_1$.
Test the answer against $\pm V_{\text{sat}}$ rails before finalizing.
Recall the 741 numbers as the practical counterweight.
